iec-230-400.name: IEC 230/400 V, 50 Hz, three-phase wye
iec-230-400.toleranceRef: EN 50160 / IEC 60038: ±10 % at supply terminals (95 % of 10 min values); all 10 min values +10 % / −15 %

iec-220-380.name: Legacy 220/380 V, 50 Hz
iec-220-380.toleranceRef: National; often treated as IEC 60038 230 V family in practice

na-split.name: North American 120/240 V split-phase, 60 Hz
na-split.toleranceRef: ANSI C84.1 Range A service ±5 % (114–126 V / 228–252 V); utilization +5 % / −10 %

na-wye-480.name: North American 480Y/277 V, 60 Hz (large commercial / industrial)
na-wye-480.toleranceRef: ANSI C84.1. 277 V is L–N of 480 V wye — lighting and some workplace EVSE, not residential. Canada analogue 600Y/347 V.

it-230.name: 230 V IT (line-to-line), 50 Hz, often no distributed neutral

br-mixed.name: Brazil mixed 127/220 V, 60 Hz
br-mixed.toleranceRef: ANEEL / NBR; typically ±5 to ±10 % by utility

countries.name: Albania
countries.notes: IT pockets similar to Norway.

countries.name: Austria
countries.notes: Three-phase dwellings common; 11 kW default wallbox.

countries.name: Belgium
countries.notes: Some areas 3×230 V delta without neutral — EVSE that need N–PE bond are problematic.

countries.name: Denmark
countries.notes: Mode 1 restricted. High share of 3-phase homes.

countries.name: Finland
countries.notes: Three-phase 3×25 A typical apartment/house service.

countries.name: France
countries.notes: NF C 15-100. Residential TT with local electrode + 30 mA RCD. Single-phase 7.4 kW common.

countries.name: Germany
countries.notes: DIN VDE 0100-722, VDE-AR-N 4100. 11 kW (3×16 A) is the residential sweet spot; 22 kW needs 3×32 A and grid-operator notification.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.notes: Similar PME open-PEN issue to the UK. Homes mostly single-phase.

countries.name: Italy
countries.notes: Mode 1 public charging prohibited. Type 3 legacy. 3 kW / 6 kW contractual limits common in apartments.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.notes: 3×25 A or 3×35 A household connections common; 11 kW standard.

countries.name: Norway
countries.notes: IT: 230 V L–L, often no N. 1φ charging 3.7–7.4 kW. 3φ IT only if the car supports it (~11 kW at ~28 A). Newer buildings TN 400 V → 11/22 kW.

countries.name: Spain
countries.notes: ITC-BT-52. Many apartments limited contracted power.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.notes: Three-phase 3×16 A or 3×20 A typical.

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.notes: NIV / NIN. Mode 1 restricted. Type J household 10 A; 16 A Type J variant exists.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.earth: TN-C-S (PME); TT rural; TN-S some urban
countries.notes: BS 7671 Section 722. Mostly 1φ 60–100 A. Open-PEN (O-PEN) protection or TT island required for outdoor PME charging. Voltage historically 230 V +10/−6 % (216–253 V).

countries.name: United States
countries.notes: Homes: 120/240 V split-phase. Level 1 120 V; Level 2 240 V 32–48 A; 125 % breaker (NEC 625). Apartments often 208Y/120 (Level 2 at 208 V, −13 %). Large commercial: 480Y/277 V — 277 V is L–N of 480 V wye (lighting / some workplace AC EVSE), not residential; 80 A @ 277 V ≈ 22 kW AC; DCFC on 480 V 3φ. Also 480 V delta (no 277 V) and high-leg 240 V delta (never L–N EVSE on the high leg). J1772/NACS 1φ only.

countries.name: Canada
countries.notes: CEC. Homes 120/240 V like the US. Apartments 208Y/120. Large commercial often 600Y/347 V (347 V lighting = 277 V analogue) as well as 480Y/277. Cold-weather derating of outdoor cables. Same J1772/NACS 1φ picture.

countries.name: Mexico
countries.notes: 127/220 V split-phase common — not US 120/240 V. Commercial may be 220 V 3φ or 480Y/277. NOM, not NEC. J1772/NACS.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.notes: NBR IEC 61851. Voltage 127 or 220 V by state. Type 2 AC emerging; some J1772 imports.

countries.name: Argentina
countries.notes: Type I polarity reversed vs AU/CN.

countries.name: Colombia
countries.notes: 120/208 V common.

countries.name: China
countries.notes: GB/T 18487, 20234.2. Voltage +7/−10 % (GB/T 12325). Home AC piles typically 7 kW 1φ 32 A. Separate DC inlet.

countries.name: Japan
countries.notes: East 50 Hz, west 60 Hz. Home EV charging on 200 V single-phase. Type 1 AC; CHAdeMO is DC only.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.notes: 220 V 60 Hz. AC historically Type 1; Type 2 / CCS2 growing on European models.

countries.name: Hong Kong
countries.notes: BS 1363 sockets. Apartment charging dominated by building EVSE.

countries.name: India
countries.notes: IS 17017. 4-wheel AC is Type 2. 2/3-wheel Bharat AC-001 uses IEC 60309. Wide voltage variation in practice.

countries.name: Singapore
countries.notes: SS 638. Type 2 Mode 3.

countries.name: Vietnam
countries.notes: Imported Chinese vehicles may keep GB/T.

countries.name: Philippines
countries.notes: 220 V 60 Hz single-phase typical; no 110 V despite Type A plugs.

countries.name: Australia
countries.notes: AS/NZS 3000, SA TS 5396. Most houses 1φ 63 A → 7.4 kW. Three-phase houses 11/22 kW. WA historically 240 V.

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.notes: SNZ PAS 6011. Voltage limits widened to 230 V ±10 % (2025). Mostly single-phase homes.

countries.name: United Arab Emirates
countries.notes: Villas often 3-phase; Type 2 wallboxes common.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
countries.notes: 60 Hz (unlike most 230 V countries). SASO. Type 2.

countries.name: Israel
countries.notes: Mode 1 not allowed.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.notes: SANS 10142-1. MEN-like PME. Load-shedding: EVSE should ride through voltage dips or inhibit cleanly.

countries.name: Nigeria
countries.notes: Wide practical voltage variation; design EVSE for full IEC ±10 % plus margin.

countries.name: Russia
countries.notes: GOST / IEC dual. Three-phase dwellings common in cities. Type 2 AC.

countries.name: Belarus
countries.notes: Some Chinese-market vehicles keep GB/T AC.

countries.name: Pakistan
countries.notes: Wide practical voltage swing; specify full IEC band plus margin.
